html: שׁרשׁ (appar. √ of foll.; Di Jb 40, 16 Buhl al. think = שׁרשׁר, √ שׁרר, cf. שֹׁר, etc., Ethiopic ሥrው: nerve, muscle, whence שֹׁרֶשׁ as root-fibre, but word very ancient, and this der. quite unproven; < SchwallyZMG iii (1898), 140 f. cp. Arabic شَرْسٌ (ش by dissimilation), thorn-bush, شَرْسٌ hard, rough, rugged (of ground), شَرِسَ ill-natured, cross; hence שֹׁרֶשׁ, from tough, gnarled root-fibres; NH and Ph. שרש, Assyrian šuršu, all root, Sab. שרס (v. Arabic supr.) root, foundation HomChr 124, אשרס foundation DHMZMG xxix (1875), 606; xxxvii (1883), 415; Aramaic שׁוֹרְשָׁא, ܫܶܪܫܳܐ root).
